scenarios.title: A Child Is Missing. Every Minute Counts.
scenarios.description: The resources may already exist. The challenge is making the whole system act as one.

scenarios.title: The Patient Nobody Sees as a Whole.
scenarios.description: Every professional may do their job correctly while the patient still falls through the interfaces between them.

scenarios.title: Four Agencies, One Threat, No Shared Picture.
scenarios.description: A crisis can cross jurisdictions faster than organizations can align facts, commands and public warnings.

scenarios.title: The Heat Wave Is Here. Who Checks the People Most at Risk?
scenarios.description: An alert is not a response plan until somebody is responsible for reaching the person who may not survive it.

scenarios.title: During the Cyberattack, Six Teams Work in Six Different Realities.
scenarios.description: The technical incident is only half the crisis; the other half is keeping security, operations, leadership, communications and partners synchronized.

scenarios.title: The Warning Loses Its Meaning on the Way Up.
scenarios.description: A critical message can arrive at the top stripped of the uncertainty and reasoning that made it urgent.

scenarios.title: Eighty-Seven Complaints. The System Sees Eighty-Seven Files, Not One Crisis.
scenarios.description: Individual reports can be weak. Their pattern can be overwhelming.

scenarios.title: The Lab Knows the Water Is Dangerous. Who Must Know Next?
scenarios.description: A critical result is not safe merely because somebody received it.

scenarios.title: The Expert Retires Friday.
scenarios.description: Thirty years of judgment should not leave the building in one cardboard box.

scenarios.title: The Professor's Best Course Disappears with the Account.
scenarios.description: A lifetime of teaching improvement should become a reusable asset, not an abandoned folder.

scenarios.title: The Student's Best Work Dies After the Grade.
scenarios.description: A university can produce thousands of prototypes and investigations every year yet accumulate almost no operational memory from them.

scenarios.title: Publish the Trade Before the Last Master Leaves.
scenarios.description: Skills that live only in hands and stories can vanish faster than institutions realize.

scenarios.title: The Failed Experiment Nobody Can Learn From.
scenarios.description: When only success becomes visible, everyone else can unknowingly pay to repeat the same failure.

scenarios.title: The Expertise Exists. The Right People Never Meet.
scenarios.description: Complex problems are often organized by department even when the solution requires a temporary community of expertise.

scenarios.title: The Family Sees the Change Before the System Does.
scenarios.description: Lived familiarity can reveal deterioration before a formal measurement does.

scenarios.title: Residents Keep Warning. The Institution Stops Hearing.
scenarios.description: When persistent complainants are classified as a nuisance, the organization can erase the feedback channel that reveals systemic risk.

scenarios.title: Local Knowledge Never Enters the Decision.
scenarios.description: A technically correct plan can still fail when it excludes the people who understand the place, practice or community it will change.

scenarios.title: A Charismatic Claim Travels Faster Than the Evidence.
scenarios.description: One confident voice can look like one side of a debate even when the underlying evidence is profoundly asymmetric.

scenarios.title: The Risk Is Real. So Is the Benefit.
scenarios.description: Trust improves when known harms are put at the right scale instead of denied or sensationalized.

scenarios.title: The Miracle Cure Goes Viral Before the Trials Finish.
scenarios.description: Early plausibility is not the same thing as demonstrated benefit.

scenarios.title: Doubt Can Be Manufactured Faster Than Causality Can Be Explained.
scenarios.description: Complex evidence is expensive to build. A misleading counter-claim can be cheap to repeat.

scenarios.title: One Cold Day Against a Century of Measurements.
scenarios.description: A vivid anecdote is cognitively stronger than a statistical distribution unless the evidence system makes scale visible.

scenarios.title: A Billion-Dollar Project. Nobody Can Reconstruct Why.
scenarios.description: Costs, requirements and risks change for years; the institution must still be able to explain each major turn.

scenarios.title: Experts Should Inform the Decision, Not Own It.
scenarios.description: A society needs expertise without turning expertise into unaccountable sovereignty.

scenarios.title: Make the Unpopular Decision Reconstructible.
scenarios.description: A difficult decision may remain controversial; it should not become impossible to understand.

scenarios.title: Make the Trade-Offs Visible Before Choosing.
scenarios.description: When every option wins on a different metric, the real decision is which values and risks receive priority.

scenarios.title: Twenty Thousand People Participate. Then Nothing Happens.
scenarios.description: Participation without a governed path to decision and execution can create engagement while destroying trust.

scenarios.title: Another Disaster. Another Forgotten Report.
scenarios.description: Learning fails when recommendations become documents instead of obligations with owners, deadlines and evidence of closure.

scenarios.title: Replay the Cyberattack Without Inventing Hindsight.
scenarios.description: A post-mortem is misleading if it judges yesterday’s decisions using information that only became available today.

scenarios.title: New Audit. New Names. Same Risk.
scenarios.description: An organization can produce repeated findings without building the memory that makes recurrence visible before the next failure.

scenarios.title: The Dashboard Is Green. A Small Group Is Still Falling Through.
scenarios.description: Average improvement can hide severe failure concentrated in a smaller population.

scenarios.title: The Government Keeps Buying Back Its Own Knowledge.
scenarios.description: Outside expertise should leave the public institution more capable, not more dependent.

scenarios.title: The Municipality Depends on a System It Cannot Inspect or Leave.
scenarios.description: A useful system can still become a source of domination when the institution cannot understand, contest, repair or exit it.

scenarios.title: Nobody Knows Why the Legacy System Works This Way.
scenarios.description: A system can remain operational long after the decisions, people and documentation that made it understandable are gone.

scenarios.title: Digitized Culture Without Context Becomes Raw Material.
scenarios.description: Preservation without provenance, authority and rights can turn living culture into extractable data.

scenarios.title: Essential Work Must Continue When the Network Does Not.
scenarios.description: Critical knowledge and coordination should not disappear because one cloud service, vendor or connection is unavailable.
